note: Chemistry round 4: two data passages (iron/copper displacement, pH table) and applied items across all fifteen topics, taking Chemistry past 500 curated questions.

passages.title: Reaction of iron filings with copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI)
passages.text:
Excess iron filings were added to 100 cm³
of 0.50 mol/dm³ copper(II)
tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution in a beaker
and stirred until the blue colour
disappeared. The temperature and the mass
of solid in the beaker were recorded.
(Fe = 56, Cu = 64)

Reading                      Value
Initial temperature (°C)      27.0
Final temperature (°C)        34.5
Mass of iron added (g)        5.60
Mass of solid at end (g)      6.00

passages.title: pH of some household and laboratory solutions
passages.text:
The pH of several solutions was measured
with a pH meter at 25 °C. The results are
shown below.

Solution                    pH
Lime juice                  2.2
Rain water                  5.6
Pure water                  7.0
Baking soda solution        8.4
Household bleach           12.5

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the experiment above, the blue colour of the solution disappeared because
questions.A: the copper(II) ions were reduced to copper metal by the iron
questions.B: the iron filings absorbed the blue dye from the solution
questions.C: the tetraoxosulphate(VI) ions were destroyed by the iron
questions.D: the solution evaporated as the temperature rose
questions.explanation: Fe(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Fe²⁺(aq) + Cu(s): the blue Cu²⁺ ions are replaced by pale green Fe²⁺ ions and reddish-brown copper is deposited.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the experiment above, the number of moles of copper(II) ions that reacted was

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the experiment above, the mass of iron that dissolved was
questions.explanation: One mole of iron reacts per mole of Cu²⁺: 0.05 × 56 = 2.8 g of iron dissolved.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the experiment above, the mass of solid at the end (6.00 g) is greater than the mass of iron added because
questions.A: the iron rusted and gained oxygen from the air
questions.B: the tetraoxosulphate(VI) crystallised out on the iron
questions.C: water of crystallisation was absorbed by the iron
questions.D: each 56 g of iron dissolved was replaced by 64 g of copper deposited
questions.explanation: 2.8 g of iron dissolved but 0.05 × 64 = 3.2 g of copper was deposited; 5.60 − 2.8 + 3.2 = 6.00 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The rise in temperature recorded in the experiment above shows that the reaction is
questions.explanation: Heat is given out to the solution, raising its temperature from 27.0 °C to 34.5 °C, so the reaction is exothermic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction studied above, iron acts as
questions.explanation: Iron loses electrons (Fe → Fe²⁺ + 2e⁻) and gives them to the copper(II) ions, so it is oxidised and is the reducing agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the table above, the solution with the highest hydrogen ion concentration is
questions.explanation: The lower the pH, the higher the hydrogen ion concentration; lime juice (pH 2.2) is the most acidic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the table above, the ratio of the hydrogen ion concentration in rain water to that in pure water is approximately

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Rain water in the table above has a pH below 7 because it contains dissolved
questions.D: carbon(IV) oxide forming a weak acid
questions.explanation: CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃, a weak acid, so even unpolluted rain is slightly acidic (about pH 5.6).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Methyl orange is red below pH 3.1 and yellow above pH 4.4. From the table above, the solutions in which methyl orange would appear yellow are
questions.A: lime juice and rain water only
questions.B: rain water and pure water only
questions.C: all the solutions except lime juice
questions.D: baking soda solution and bleach only
questions.explanation: Every solution in the table except lime juice (pH 2.2) has a pH above 4.4, so methyl orange is yellow in rain water, pure water, baking soda solution and bleach.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the table above, the hydroxide ion concentration in household bleach is approximately

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Baking soda solution (pH 8.4 in the table above) is used to relieve acid indigestion because it
questions.A: is a strong alkali that destroys the stomach lining
questions.B: lowers the pH of the stomach contents further
questions.C: dissolves the food in the stomach more quickly
questions.D: neutralises excess hydrochloric acid in the stomach
questions.explanation: Sodium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV) is a mild base: NaHCO₃ + HCl → NaCl + H₂O + CO₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A balloon filled with 2.0 dm³ of helium at 27 °C and 1.0 atm rises to a height where the temperature is −23 °C and the pressure 0.5 atm. Its volume there is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ammonia and hydrogen chloride gases are released at the same time from opposite ends of a 1 m glass tube. The white ring of ammonium chloride forms
questions.A: exactly in the middle of the tube
questions.explanation: Ammonia (M = 17) diffuses faster than hydrogen chloride (M = 36.5), so it travels further before the gases meet.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 50 cm³ of oxygen diffuses through a porous pot in 40 s. The time for 50 cm³ of a gas of relative molecular mass 128 to diffuse under the same conditions is (O₂ = 32)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The smell of perfume opened at one end of a room soon reaches the other end. This is because the perfume molecules
questions.A: are attracted by the walls of the room
questions.B: react with the air to form a gas
questions.C: are carried only by the light in the room
questions.D: diffuse through the air by random motion
questions.explanation: Gas molecules move randomly and spread from where they are concentrated to where they are not — diffusion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A cylinder of fixed volume contains a gas at 2.0 atm and 27 °C. The temperature at which the pressure becomes 3.0 atm is
questions.explanation: P/T is constant: T₂ = 300 × 3.0/2.0 = 450 K = 177 °C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements about real gases is correct?
questions.A: they behave most ideally at high pressure and low temperature
questions.B: there are no forces at all between their molecules
questions.C: their molecules have zero volume at all temperatures
questions.D: they behave most ideally at low pressure and high temperature
questions.explanation: At low pressure the molecules are far apart, and at high temperature they move too fast for the weak attractions to matter, so the ideal-gas assumptions nearly hold.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Naphthalene balls kept in a wardrobe gradually become smaller and disappear without leaving a liquid. This is because naphthalene
questions.A: melts and then evaporates very quickly
questions.C: dissolves in the moisture of the air
questions.D: sublimes directly from solid to vapour
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas; iodine and ammonium chloride behave similarly.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A chemist finds that 112 cm³ of an unknown gas, measured at s.t.p., has a mass of 0.16 g. The gas is most likely (molar volume = 22,400 cm³; H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, S = 32)
questions.explanation: Moles = 112/22,400 = 0.005; M = 0.16/0.005 = 32, the relative molecular mass of oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Crystals of copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) are best obtained from its solution by
questions.A: boiling the solution to dryness over a strong flame
questions.B: adding a large volume of cold water and stirring
questions.C: filtering the solution through fine filter paper
questions.D: evaporating the solution to saturation and allowing it to cool slowly
questions.explanation: Slow cooling of a saturated solution gives large, well-formed crystals; boiling to dryness gives a powder and drives off water of crystallisation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A liquid boils at 80 °C at sea level. On a high mountain where the atmospheric pressure is lower, it boils at
questions.explanation: A liquid boils when its vapour pressure equals the external pressure; a lower external pressure is reached at a lower temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following mixtures can be separated by using a separating funnel?
questions.explanation: Kerosene and water are immiscible liquids that form two layers; the lower layer is run off through the tap.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting produces a new substance (hydrated iron(III) oxide) and cannot easily be reversed; the others are physical changes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Salt is separated from a solution of salt in water by evaporation rather than by filtration because
questions.A: dissolved salt particles are too small to be trapped by filter paper
questions.B: salt particles are too heavy to be held back by filter paper
questions.C: filter paper dissolves in salt solution
questions.D: evaporation is always faster than filtration
questions.explanation: A true solution contains ions or molecules that pass straight through filter paper; only insoluble solids are filtered off.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An element has two isotopes, ⁶³X (69%) and ⁶⁵X (31%). Its relative atomic mass is approximately

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The species ⁴⁰₁₈Ar, ⁴⁰₂₀Ca²⁺ and ³⁹₁₉K⁺ all have the same
questions.explanation: Ar has 18 electrons; Ca²⁺ has 20 − 2 = 18; K⁺ has 19 − 1 = 18. They are isoelectronic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The maximum number of electrons that can occupy the third shell (n = 3) of an atom is
questions.explanation: The maximum is 2n² = 2 × 3² = 18 (the 3s, 3p and 3d sub-shells together).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following electronic configurations represents an atom in an excited state?
questions.explanation: In 1s² 2s² 2p⁵ 3s¹ an electron occupies 3s while 2p is still incomplete; the ground state of that atom (neon) would be 1s² 2s² 2p⁶.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The atomic number of an element is 24. The number of electrons in its 3d sub-shell is
questions.explanation: Chromium is exceptional: its configuration is [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹, a half-filled d sub-shell being especially stable.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The energy of an electron in an atom is lowest when the electron is in the
questions.explanation: Electrons closest to the nucleus are most strongly attracted and have the lowest (most negative) energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements about cathode rays is correct?
questions.A: they are positively charged and heavy
questions.B: they cannot be deflected by a magnetic field
questions.C: they are electromagnetic waves like light
questions.D: they are streams of electrons, deflected towards a positive plate
questions.explanation: Thomson showed that cathode rays are negatively charged particles (electrons) with the same charge-to-mass ratio whatever gas or cathode metal is used.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A nuclide ²²⁶₈₈X emits an alpha particle and the daughter nuclide then emits a beta particle. The final nuclide has
questions.explanation: Alpha emission: 88 → 86, 226 → 222; beta emission then raises the atomic number to 87 with the mass number unchanged.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following radiations has the greatest penetrating power?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays are high-energy electromagnetic waves stopped only by thick lead or concrete; alpha particles are stopped by paper.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A radioactive element has a half-life of 30 minutes. The time taken for its activity to fall to 12.5% of its original value is
questions.explanation: 12.5% = 1/8 = (½)³, three half-lives: 3 × 30 = 90 minutes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Nuclear fission differs from ordinary chemical reactions in that fission
questions.A: changes one element into different elements
questions.B: involves only the outermost electrons of the atoms
questions.C: releases far less energy per atom
questions.D: never produces radiation of any kind
questions.explanation: In fission the nucleus itself splits into nuclei of lighter elements; chemical reactions rearrange electrons and leave every nucleus unchanged.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of protons, neutrons and electrons in the ion ³²₁₆S²⁻ are respectively
questions.explanation: Protons = 16; neutrons = 32 − 16 = 16; the 2− charge means two extra electrons: 16 + 2 = 18.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Elements A, B, C and D have atomic numbers 8, 11, 16 and 17 respectively. The pair of elements with the most similar chemical properties is
questions.explanation: A (2,6) and C (2,8,6) both have six outer electrons and belong to Group 6; B (2,8,1) is in Group 1 and D (2,8,7) in Group 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Going down Group 7 (the halogens), the elements change at room temperature from
questions.explanation: Fluorine and chlorine are gases, bromine is a liquid and iodine is a solid; van der Waals forces increase with molecular size.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The first ionisation energies of Na, Mg and Al are 496, 738 and 578 kJ/mol. The value for aluminium is lower than that for magnesium because
questions.A: the outer electron of aluminium is in a 3p orbital, further out and shielded by the 3s electrons
questions.B: the nuclear charge of aluminium is smaller than that of magnesium, so its electrons are held less firmly
questions.C: aluminium is a poorer conductor than magnesium, so its electrons are less mobile in the solid
questions.D: the aluminium atom has a much larger radius than the magnesium atom because it has extra shells
questions.explanation: Al: [Ne] 3s² 3p¹; the 3p electron is higher in energy and more easily removed than one of the paired 3s electrons of Mg.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following elements is a noble gas?
questions.explanation: Argon (Group 0) has a complete outer shell of eight electrons and is chemically inert.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The oxides of period 3 elements change across the period from
questions.explanation: Na₂O and MgO are basic, Al₂O₃ is amphoteric, and SiO₂, P₄O₁₀, SO₃ and Cl₂O₇ are acidic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An element forms a chloride of formula XCl₂ and an oxide XO that dissolves in water to give an alkaline solution. X is most likely
questions.explanation: A metal of Group 2 forms a +2 ion; CaO dissolves in water to give calcium hydroxide (lime water).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Element X (atomic number 19) and element Y (atomic number 35) combine to form a compound. The formula and bond type of the compound are
questions.explanation: X is potassium (Group 1, forms X⁺) and Y is bromine (Group 7, forms Y⁻); they form the ionic compound KBr.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ions has the smallest ionic radius?
questions.explanation: All four are isoelectronic (10 electrons); Al³⁺ has the greatest nuclear charge (13) pulling the same electrons closest.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A group of elements have the electronic configurations ns² np⁵. They
questions.A: readily gain one electron to form negative ions
questions.B: readily lose one electron to form positive ions
questions.C: are inert and form no compounds
questions.D: form ions with a charge of 2+
questions.explanation: One electron short of a full shell, these halogens gain an electron to form X⁻ ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The elements of period 3 in order of increasing electronegativity are
questions.A: Na < Mg < Al < Si < P < S < Cl
questions.B: Cl < S < P < Si < Al < Mg < Na
questions.C: Na < Al < Mg < Si < S < P < Cl
questions.D: Ar < Cl < S < P < Si < Al < Mg
questions.explanation: Electronegativity rises across a period as the nuclear charge increases and the atomic radius shrinks; argon is not assigned a value.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which pair of elements would react most violently with each other?
questions.explanation: Caesium is the most reactive common metal (largest atom, outer electron most easily lost) and fluorine the most reactive non-metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Transition elements are able to act as catalysts mainly because they
questions.A: are very dense and have high melting points
questions.D: can exist in several oxidation states
questions.explanation: Variable oxidation states let a transition metal accept and donate electrons readily, providing an alternative reaction path (e.g. Fe in the Haber process, V₂O₅ in the Contact process).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Magnesium oxide has a much higher melting point (2,852 °C) than sodium chloride (801 °C) because
questions.A: Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ ions carry double charges, so the electrostatic attraction in the lattice is much stronger
questions.B: magnesium oxide is covalent while sodium chloride is ionic
questions.C: sodium chloride contains water of crystallisation
questions.D: magnesium oxide molecules are much heavier than sodium chloride molecules
questions.explanation: Lattice energy increases with the product of the ionic charges; (2+)(2−) gives roughly four times the attraction of (1+)(1−).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following molecules is linear?
questions.explanation: Carbon in CO₂ has two double bonds and no lone pairs, so the molecule is linear (O=C=O, 180°).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The bond angle in methane, CH₄, is
questions.explanation: Four bonding pairs and no lone pairs around carbon repel equally, giving a regular tetrahedron with 109.5° angles.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The bond angle in water (104.5°) is smaller than that in ammonia (107°) because
questions.A: oxygen is a larger atom than nitrogen, so its bonds lie further apart
questions.B: water has fewer hydrogen atoms, so the bonds have more room to spread
questions.C: water has two lone pairs which repel the bonding pairs more strongly
questions.D: the O–H bond is longer than the N–H bond and bends more easily
questions.explanation: Lone pair–lone pair repulsion is greater than lone pair–bond pair repulsion, so the two lone pairs on oxygen squeeze the bonds closer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following substances is held together by van der Waals forces only?
questions.explanation: Dry ice consists of separate CO₂ molecules attracted only by weak intermolecular forces, which is why it sublimes at −78 °C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hydrogen chloride is a covalent gas, yet its aqueous solution conducts electricity because
questions.A: water molecules pull the HCl molecules apart into H₃O⁺ and Cl⁻ ions
questions.B: the gas contains free ions even before it dissolves
questions.C: water itself is a good conductor of electricity
questions.D: chlorine atoms lose electrons to the water
questions.explanation: The polar H–Cl bond breaks heterolytically in water: HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻, and the mobile ions carry the current.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Tetrachloromethane (CCl₄) does not dissolve in water because
questions.A: it is a non-polar molecule while water is polar
questions.B: its molecules are too heavy to mix with water
questions.explanation: Water's hydrogen bonds are not compensated by any attraction to the non-polar CCl₄ molecules, so the two liquids do not mix.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following contains a coordinate (dative covalent) bond?
questions.explanation: In NH₄⁺ the nitrogen lone pair forms the fourth N–H bond by donating both electrons to a proton.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The electron-pair geometry around the central atom in ammonia is tetrahedral, but the molecule is described as pyramidal because
questions.A: one of the four positions is occupied by a lone pair, which is not counted in the shape
questions.B: nitrogen can only form three bonds at right angles
questions.C: the three hydrogen atoms lie in the same plane as nitrogen
questions.D: the N–H bonds are double bonds
questions.explanation: Shape describes the positions of atoms only; the lone pair sits at one tetrahedral corner, leaving a trigonal pyramid of atoms with 107° angles.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of elements would form a covalent compound?
questions.explanation: Two non-metals with similar electronegativities share electrons; the other pairs are metal + non-metal and form ionic compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is soluble in water but hexane (C₆H₁₄) is not. This is because ethanol
questions.A: has a lower relative molecular mass than hexane
questions.B: has a higher boiling point than hexane
questions.C: is an ionic compound while hexane is covalent
questions.D: can form hydrogen bonds with water molecules through its –OH group
questions.explanation: The polar –OH group hydrogen-bonds with water; hexane has only non-polar C–H and C–C bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following properties is characteristic of a metallic bond?
questions.A: electrons are transferred from one atom to another
questions.B: electrons are shared between pairs of atoms
questions.C: positive ions are held in a sea of delocalised electrons
questions.D: the bond is formed only between two different elements
questions.explanation: The mobile electrons account for the conductivity, lustre and malleability of metals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The volume of 0.20 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid that contains 0.73 g of HCl is (HCl = 36.5)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A sample of hydrated sodium tetraoxosulphate(VI), Na₂SO₄·xH₂O, of mass 3.22 g gave 1.42 g of the anhydrous salt on heating. The value of x is (Na₂SO₄ = 142, H₂O = 18)
questions.explanation: Anhydrous salt: 1.42/142 = 0.01 mol; water lost: 1.80/18 = 0.10 mol; ratio 1 : 10, so x = 10.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The mass of silver deposited by the same quantity of electricity that deposits 3.2 g of copper is (Cu = 64, Ag = 108)
questions.explanation: 3.2 g Cu = 0.05 mol, needing 0.1 mol of electrons; Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag, so 0.1 mol = 10.8 g of silver.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 10 cm³ of a gaseous hydrocarbon required 30 cm³ of oxygen for complete combustion and produced 20 cm³ of carbon(IV) oxide (all volumes at the same temperature and pressure). The hydrocarbon is
questions.explanation: Gay-Lussac: CₓHᵧ + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + …; 2 carbons use 2 O₂ for CO₂, the remaining O₂ forms 2H₂O, so y = 4: C₂H₄.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of ions in 0.5 mol of aluminium chloride, AlCl₃, when fully dissociated is (Avogadro's number = 6.0 × 10²³)
questions.explanation: Each formula unit gives 4 ions (1 Al³⁺ + 3 Cl⁻): 0.5 × 4 × 6.0 × 10²³ = 1.2 × 10²⁴.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 50 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ NaOH is added to 50 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ H₂SO₄. The resulting solution is
questions.A: acidic, because half of the acid remains unreacted
questions.C: alkaline, because the base is in excess
questions.D: acidic, because sodium tetraoxosulphate(VI) is an acid salt
questions.explanation: H₂SO₄ needs 2 mol of NaOH per mole; 0.005 mol of NaOH neutralises only 0.0025 mol of the 0.005 mol of acid present.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The relative molecular mass of a gas that has a vapour density of 32 is
questions.explanation: Relative molecular mass = 2 × vapour density = 64.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 0.1 mol of a metal M reacted with excess acid, 2,240 cm³ of hydrogen was liberated at s.t.p. The valency of M is (molar volume = 22.4 dm³)
questions.explanation: 2,240 cm³ = 0.1 mol H₂ = 0.2 mol of H atoms displaced by 0.1 mol of M, so each atom of M supplies 2 electrons: valency 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The mass of oxygen gas that contains the same number of molecules as 14 g of nitrogen gas is (N = 14, O = 16)
questions.explanation: 14 g of N₂ = 0.5 mol; 0.5 mol of O₂ = 0.5 × 32 = 16 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction 2Al + 3Cl₂ → 2AlCl₃, 5.4 g of aluminium is mixed with 14.2 g of chlorine. The limiting reagent and the mass of AlCl₃ formed are (Al = 27, Cl = 35.5)
questions.explanation: Al = 0.2 mol, Cl₂ = 14.2/71 = 0.2 mol; 0.2 mol Cl₂ needs only 0.133 mol Al, so chlorine runs out first and gives 0.2 × 2/3 = 0.133 mol AlCl₃ = 0.133 × 133.5 = 17.8 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The concentration in g/dm³ of a 0.25 mol/dm³ solution of potassium hydroxide is (KOH = 56)
questions.explanation: Concentration in g/dm³ = molar concentration × molar mass = 0.25 × 56 = 14 g/dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many moles of hydrogen atoms are present in 0.25 mol of ethanol, C₂H₅OH?
questions.explanation: Each molecule of C₂H₆O contains 6 hydrogen atoms: 0.25 × 6 = 1.5 mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements describes a strong acid?
questions.A: an acid with a very high concentration
questions.B: an acid that reacts quickly with all metals
questions.C: an acid that is completely ionised in aqueous solution
questions.D: an acid whose solution has a pH of about 5
questions.explanation: Strength refers to the degree of ionisation, not the concentration; a dilute solution of HCl is still a strong acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A 0.1 mol/dm³ solution of ethanoic acid has a pH of about 3 while 0.1 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid has a pH of 1. Which statement is correct?
questions.A: ethanoic acid is more concentrated than hydrochloric acid
questions.B: both acids release the same number of hydrogen ions
questions.C: hydrochloric acid is a weaker acid than ethanoic acid
questions.D: ethanoic acid is only slightly ionised in water
questions.explanation: The same concentration gives 100 times fewer H⁺ ions in the ethanoic acid solution, showing that only a small fraction of its molecules ionise.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The volume of 0.5 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide needed to neutralise 25 cm³ of 0.2 mol/dm³ tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is
questions.explanation: Moles of acid = 0.2 × 0.025 = 0.005; NaOH needed = 0.01 mol; volume = 0.01/0.5 = 0.02 dm³ = 20 cm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following salts is a normal salt?
questions.explanation: A normal salt has all the replaceable hydrogen of the acid replaced by a metal; the others still contain replaceable hydrogen (acid salts).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Zinc oxide is described as amphoteric because it
questions.A: reacts with both acids and alkalis to form salts
questions.C: dissolves in water to give a neutral solution
questions.D: reacts with neither acids nor alkalis
questions.explanation: ZnO + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂O and ZnO + 2NaOH + H₂O → Na₂Zn(OH)₄; Al₂O₃ and PbO behave similarly.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a basic salt?
questions.explanation: A basic salt contains hydroxide or oxide ions as well as the normal anion, e.g. Zn(OH)Cl and Pb(OH)NO₃.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A double salt is exemplified by
questions.explanation: A double salt crystallises from a solution of two simple salts and gives both sets of ions in solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A solution of sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) turns red litmus blue although it contains no hydroxide. This is because
questions.A: trioxocarbonate(IV) ions react with water to form hydroxide ions
questions.C: the salt contains free sodium hydroxide
questions.D: carbon(IV) oxide gas escapes and leaves an alkali
questions.explanation: CO₃²⁻ + H₂O ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻ (salt hydrolysis) makes the solution alkaline.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following indicators is most suitable for the titration of a strong acid against a weak base such as ammonia?
questions.explanation: The end point of a strong acid–weak base titration is on the acidic side (pH about 5), within the range of methyl orange (3.1–4.4).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following oxides is neutral?
questions.explanation: CO (like N₂O and H₂O) reacts with neither acids nor bases; SO₂ is acidic, CaO basic and Al₂O₃ amphoteric.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Anhydrous calcium chloride left in an open dish absorbs moisture from the air and eventually forms a solution. This behaviour is called
questions.explanation: A deliquescent substance absorbs so much water vapour that it dissolves in it; a hygroscopic substance absorbs moisture without dissolving.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct method for diluting concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid?
questions.A: add the acid slowly to the water while stirring
questions.B: pour the water quickly into the concentrated acid
questions.C: mix equal volumes of acid and water in a closed bottle
questions.D: heat the acid first and then add the water
questions.explanation: Dilution is highly exothermic; adding acid to a large volume of water spreads the heat, whereas water added to acid can boil and spit.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aqueous solution has a pOH of 3. Its pH and nature are
questions.explanation: pH + pOH = 14, so pH = 11, which is alkaline.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Lead(II) chloride is prepared by mixing solutions of lead(II) trioxonitrate(V) and sodium chloride. The pure dry salt is obtained by
questions.B: crystallising the filtrate by slow cooling
questions.C: distilling off the water and collecting the residue
questions.D: filtering, washing the residue with distilled water and drying it
questions.explanation: PbCl₂ is insoluble in cold water, so it is filtered off as a precipitate, washed free of soluble NaNO₃ and dried.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂, chlorine
questions.A: is reduced and acts as the oxidising agent
questions.B: is oxidised and acts as the reducing agent
questions.C: is reduced and acts as the reducing agent
questions.D: undergoes no change in oxidation number
questions.explanation: Cl goes from 0 to −1 (gains electrons, reduced) while Br⁻ is oxidised to Br₂; the substance reduced is the oxidising agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The oxidation number of chlorine in KClO₃ is
questions.explanation: K = +1, three O = −6; for a neutral compound Cl = +5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The oxidation number of phosphorus in the tetraoxophosphate(V) ion, PO₄³⁻, is
questions.explanation: Four O = −8; the ion charge is −3, so P − 8 = −3 and P = +5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions is a decomposition reaction?
questions.explanation: A single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances on heating.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hydrogen peroxide acts as a reducing agent in its reaction with
questions.A: potassium iodide solution, which turns brown
questions.B: iron(II) ions, which turn to iron(III)
questions.D: acidified potassium tetraoxomanganate(VII), which is decolourised
questions.explanation: H₂O₂ reduces MnO₄⁻ to Mn²⁺ and is itself oxidised to oxygen; in the other cases it oxidises the other reagent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the half-equation Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + xe⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O, the value of x is
questions.explanation: Chromium falls from +6 to +3 for each of the two atoms: 2 × 3 = 6 electrons gained.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When a piece of sodium is dropped into water it fizzes and the resulting solution turns red litmus blue. The gas and the solution are respectively
questions.explanation: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂; the alkaline sodium hydroxide turns litmus blue.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following equations is correctly balanced?
questions.explanation: 4 Fe and 6 O atoms on each side: 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and water only is called
questions.explanation: H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l) is the essential change in every neutralisation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Iron(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution slowly turns from green to yellow-brown on standing in air. This is because
questions.A: iron(II) ions are oxidised to iron(III) ions by oxygen
questions.B: the water evaporates and concentrates the solution
questions.C: iron(II) ions are reduced to iron metal
questions.D: carbon(IV) oxide in the air forms iron(II) trioxocarbonate(IV)
questions.explanation: Fe²⁺ is easily oxidised to Fe³⁺ (yellow-brown) by dissolved oxygen, which is why freshly prepared solution is used in tests.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A metal M reacts with dilute acid to release hydrogen and its oxide is reduced by hydrogen on heating. M is most likely
questions.explanation: A metal below hydrogen (Cu, Ag, Au) gives no hydrogen with acid; a metal well above (Na, Ca) has an oxide that hydrogen cannot reduce. Iron fits both conditions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 25 cm³ of 0.02 mol/dm³ acidified KMnO₄ is exactly decolourised by 20 cm³ of an iron(II) solution. The concentration of the iron(II) solution is
questions.explanation: MnO₄⁻ reacts with 5 Fe²⁺: moles MnO₄⁻ = 0.02 × 0.025 = 0.0005; Fe²⁺ = 0.0025 mol in 20 cm³, so C = 0.0025/0.020 = 0.125 mol/dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the electrolysis of dilute tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid with platinum electrodes, the volumes of gas collected at the cathode and anode are in the ratio
questions.explanation: Cathode: 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ → 2H₂; anode: 4OH⁻ → O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻; for the same charge, twice as much hydrogen as oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: During the electrolysis of copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution with carbon electrodes, the solution gradually becomes
questions.A: more alkaline, as hydroxide ions build up round the cathode
questions.B: neutral, because the ions removed at each electrode balance
questions.C: a deeper blue, because copper ions form at the carbon anode
questions.D: acidic, because tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is left in solution
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ is deposited at the cathode and OH⁻ is discharged as O₂ at the anode, leaving H⁺ and SO₄²⁻ ions, i.e. H₂SO₄, so the blue fades and the pH falls.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the electrolysis of copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution with copper electrodes, the anode
questions.A: loses mass as copper dissolves into the solution
questions.B: gains mass as copper is deposited on it
questions.explanation: At an active copper anode, Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ occurs in preference to the discharge of OH⁻; the cathode gains an equal mass.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The mass of aluminium deposited when 3 faradays of electricity are passed through molten aluminium oxide is (Al = 27)
questions.explanation: Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al: 3 F deposits 1 mol = 27 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A current of 2 A is passed through a solution of a metal salt for 32 minutes 10 seconds and 1.28 g of the metal (relative atomic mass 64) is deposited. The charge on the metal ion is (1 F = 96,500 C)
questions.explanation: Q = 2 × 1,930 = 3,860 C = 0.04 F; moles deposited = 1.28/64 = 0.02; 0.04/0.02 = 2 electrons per ion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ions is discharged first at the cathode when a mixture of their salts in aqueous solution is electrolysed?
questions.explanation: Ions of metals lower in the electrochemical series are discharged in preference; Cu²⁺ is well below H⁺, whereas Na⁺, K⁺ and Ca²⁺ are above it.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The standard hydrogen electrode is assigned a potential of
questions.explanation: All other standard electrode potentials are measured relative to the hydrogen electrode at 1 atm, 25 °C and 1 mol/dm³ H⁺.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A student joins a magnesium rod dipping in Mg²⁺ solution to a silver rod dipping in Ag⁺ solution through a salt bridge and a voltmeter. Given E°(Mg²⁺/Mg) = −2.37 V and E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = +0.80 V, the voltmeter should read
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.80 − (−2.37) = 3.17 V.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a zinc–carbon dry cell, the zinc case acts as the
questions.explanation: Zinc dissolves as Zn²⁺, releasing electrons (Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻); the carbon rod is the positive terminal and MnO₂ the depolariser.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a factor that determines which ion is discharged at an electrode?
questions.A: the position of the ion in the electrochemical series
questions.B: the concentration of the ion in the solution
questions.explanation: Discharge depends on the electrochemical series, concentration and the electrode material; colour has no effect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A copper spoon is to be electroplated with nickel. The correct arrangement is
questions.A: spoon as cathode, nickel as anode, in nickel(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution
questions.B: spoon as anode, nickel as cathode, in nickel(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution
questions.C: spoon as cathode, nickel as anode, in copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution
questions.D: spoon as anode, nickel as cathode, in dilute tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid
questions.explanation: The object to be plated is the cathode, the plating metal is the anode (which replenishes the ions) and the electrolyte contains ions of the plating metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The electrolysis of brine (concentrated sodium chloride solution) is used industrially to produce
questions.explanation: Cl⁻ is discharged at the anode, H⁺ at the cathode, and Na⁺ and OH⁻ remain in solution as sodium hydroxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The heat of formation of water is −286 kJ/mol. The heat evolved when 4 g of hydrogen burns completely in oxygen is (H = 1)
questions.explanation: 4 g of H₂ = 2 mol, forming 2 mol of water: 2 × 286 = 572 kJ.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When solid sodium hydroxide dissolves in water the beaker becomes warm. Which statement is correct?
questions.A: ΔH is positive and the process is exothermic
questions.B: ΔH is negative and the process is endothermic
questions.C: ΔH is positive and the process is endothermic
questions.D: ΔH is negative and the process is exothermic
questions.explanation: Heat is released to the surroundings (the water warms), so the enthalpy change is negative: exothermic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Fresh milk left at 30 °C goes sour in about 10 hours. If the rate of the souring reaction doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature, the same milk kept in a refrigerator at 0 °C should stay fresh for about
questions.explanation: Cooling by three steps of 10 °C makes the reaction 2³ = 8 times slower, so the milk lasts about 8 × 10 = 80 hours.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Marble chips react with 1.0 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid. Which change would NOT increase the rate at which carbon(IV) oxide is produced?
questions.A: crushing the marble chips into powder
questions.explanation: Dilution lowers the concentration of H⁺ ions, so collisions become less frequent and the rate falls.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The activation energy of a reaction is the
questions.A: minimum energy that colliding particles must have for a reaction to occur
questions.B: energy released when the products are formed
questions.C: difference between the energies of reactants and products
questions.D: energy needed to heat the reactants to their boiling points
questions.explanation: Only collisions with energy at least equal to the activation energy lead to bond breaking and reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In an energy profile diagram the enthalpy change of a reaction is represented by the
questions.A: height of the peak above the level of the reactants
questions.B: height of the peak above the level of the products
questions.C: difference in energy between the reactants and the products
questions.D: total energy of the products measured from the baseline
questions.explanation: ΔH = H(products) − H(reactants); the height of the peak above the reactants is the activation energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements about a catalyst is correct?
questions.A: it increases the yield of product at equilibrium
questions.B: it raises the enthalpy change of the reaction
questions.C: it is used up during the reaction
questions.D: it provides an alternative reaction path with a lower activation energy
questions.explanation: A catalyst is chemically unchanged at the end and does not alter ΔH or the equilibrium position; it only makes the reaction faster.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Enzymes in the human body work best at about 37 °C. At 70 °C they stop working because
questions.A: the enzyme protein is denatured and loses its shape
questions.B: the substrate molecules move too fast to be caught
questions.C: the water in the cells boils away
questions.D: the activation energy becomes too high
questions.explanation: Heat breaks the weak bonds that hold the enzyme in its precise three-dimensional shape, destroying the active site.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Sodium thiosulphate solution reacts with dilute acid to form a yellow precipitate of sulphur. Doubling the concentration of the thiosulphate makes the cross under the flask disappear
questions.explanation: Rate is roughly proportional to concentration for this reaction, so the time taken to form the same amount of sulphur is about halved.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The entropy of a system decreases when
questions.A: ice melts to form liquid water
questions.C: steam condenses to form liquid water
questions.D: a gas expands into a larger container
questions.explanation: Condensation turns freely moving gas molecules into a more ordered liquid, reducing the disorder (entropy).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a certain reaction ΔH = +50 kJ/mol and ΔS = +200 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. The reaction becomes spontaneous (ΔG < 0) above a temperature of
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS = 0 when T = ΔH/ΔS = 50,000/200 = 250 K; above this temperature ΔG is negative.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an endothermic process?
questions.B: neutralisation of an acid by a base
questions.explanation: CaCO₃ must be heated continuously to decompose it into CaO and CO₂; heat is absorbed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), increasing the pressure
questions.A: shifts the equilibrium to the right, giving more ammonia
questions.B: shifts the equilibrium to the left
questions.C: has no effect on the position of equilibrium
questions.explanation: Four moles of gas become two; the system relieves the added pressure by favouring the side with fewer gas molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following changes alters the value of the equilibrium constant of a reaction?
questions.D: changing the concentration of a reactant
questions.explanation: K depends only on temperature; the other changes may shift the position of equilibrium but K itself stays the same.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At a certain temperature the equilibrium constant Kc for A(g) + B(g) ⇌ C(g) + D(g) is 4. If 1 mol each of A and B are mixed in a 1 dm³ vessel, the equilibrium concentration of C is
questions.explanation: x²/(1 − x)² = 4, so x/(1 − x) = 2 and x = 2/3 = 0.67 mol/dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction CaCO₃(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO₂(g) carried out in a closed vessel, the amount of CO₂ at equilibrium is increased by
questions.explanation: The decomposition is endothermic, so heating shifts it to the right; solids do not appear in the equilibrium expression, so adding or removing them has no effect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The colour of the equilibrium mixture 2NO₂(g) (brown) ⇌ N₂O₄(g) (colourless), ΔH = −57 kJ, becomes darker when the mixture is
questions.explanation: Heating favours the endothermic (reverse) direction, producing more brown NO₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the equilibrium H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g), increasing the pressure
questions.A: increases the amount of HI in the mixture
questions.B: decreases the amount of HI in the mixture
questions.C: has no effect on the position of equilibrium
questions.D: stops the forward reaction from taking place
questions.explanation: There are two moles of gas on each side, so a pressure change cannot favour either direction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a saturated solution of silver chloride in contact with the solid, adding sodium chloride solution causes
questions.D: the silver chloride to turn black
questions.explanation: Extra Cl⁻ ions push the equilibrium AgCl(s) ⇌ Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ to the left (common-ion effect), so solid is deposited.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A reversible reaction reaches equilibrium in a closed vessel. Which statement about the system is correct?
questions.A: the concentrations of reactants and products are equal
questions.C: the forward and reverse reactions occur at the same rate
questions.D: no product is being formed any more
questions.explanation: Equilibrium is dynamic: both reactions continue but at equal rates, so the concentrations stay constant (not necessarily equal).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The equilibrium constant Kc for the reaction 2A(g) ⇌ B(g) is 0.5 dm³/mol. The value of Kc for B(g) ⇌ 2A(g) at the same temperature is
questions.explanation: Reversing a reaction inverts its equilibrium constant: 1/0.5 = 2, with the units also inverted.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The solubility of a gas in water decreases when
questions.B: the pressure of the gas is increased
questions.D: the volume of water is increased
questions.explanation: Dissolving a gas is exothermic, so heating drives the gas out — which is why warm fizzy drinks go flat quickly.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A solution contains more solute than a saturated solution would normally hold at that temperature. Such a solution is
questions.explanation: A supersaturated solution is unstable; a small crystal added to it causes the excess solute to crystallise out at once.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following metals is extracted by electrolysis rather than by chemical reduction?
questions.explanation: Sodium is too reactive for carbon or hydrogen to reduce its compounds; it is obtained by electrolysing molten sodium chloride (Downs cell).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the blast furnace, limestone is added along with the iron ore and coke in order to
questions.A: act as a fuel and raise the temperature
questions.C: supply carbon(II) oxide for the reduction
questions.explanation: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂, then CaO + SiO₂ → CaSiO₃ (slag), which floats on the molten iron and is tapped off separately.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Zinc is used to galvanise iron because zinc
questions.A: is cheaper and denser than iron, so it forms a heavy coat
questions.B: is more reactive than iron and corrodes first, protecting the iron
questions.C: forms a very hard coating that cannot be scratched off the iron
questions.D: is less reactive than iron and acts only as a barrier to water
questions.explanation: Even when the coating is scratched, zinc is oxidised in place of the iron (sacrificial protection).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A metal reacts vigorously with cold water, its hydroxide is strongly alkaline and its carbonate does not decompose on gentle heating. The metal is most likely
questions.explanation: Only the alkali metals react vigorously with cold water and have thermally stable carbonates; Mg reacts only with steam and its carbonate decomposes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When copper is heated in air it becomes coated with a black solid. The black solid is
questions.explanation: 2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO; the black layer is copper(II) oxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Anhydrous white copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) is used in the laboratory to
questions.A: test for the presence of water
questions.explanation: It turns blue as it takes up water of crystallisation: CuSO₄ + 5H₂O → CuSO₄·5H₂O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following gases is collected by downward delivery (upward displacement of air)?
questions.explanation: Chlorine is much denser than air, so it sinks and fills the jar from the bottom; hydrogen and ammonia are collected by upward delivery.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hydrogen sulphide gas is passed through a solution of a salt and a black precipitate forms. The salt is most likely
questions.explanation: Pb²⁺ + H₂S → PbS (black) + 2H⁺; zinc gives a white sulphide, and Na⁺ and Mg²⁺ sulphides do not precipitate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Aluminium foil does not react noticeably with water or air although aluminium is a fairly reactive metal. This is because
questions.A: aluminium is actually below hydrogen in the activity series
questions.B: a thin, tough layer of aluminium oxide protects the surface
questions.C: aluminium foil is coated with a plastic film
questions.D: the metal is too thin for the reaction to be seen
questions.explanation: The oxide film formed instantly in air is impervious and seals the metal beneath it (anodising thickens it deliberately).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Nitrogen(IV) oxide, a brown gas, is produced when
questions.B: copper reacts with concentrated trioxonitrate(V) acid
questions.C: zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid
questions.D: sodium trioxonitrate(V) is dissolved in water
questions.explanation: Cu + 4HNO₃(conc) → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2NO₂ + 2H₂O; the brown fumes are NO₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ammonia gas is identified in the laboratory by the fact that it
questions.A: turns moist red litmus blue and gives white fumes with hydrogen chloride
questions.B: relights a glowing splint and gives white fumes with hydrogen chloride
questions.C: turns lime water milky and turns moist blue litmus paper red
questions.D: bleaches moist litmus paper and gives a pop sound with a lighted splint
questions.explanation: Ammonia is the common alkaline gas; with HCl vapour it forms a white smoke of ammonium chloride.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an allotrope of carbon?
questions.explanation: Diamond, graphite and the fullerenes are allotropes: different structural forms of the element carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Rhombic and monoclinic sulphur are
questions.explanation: Both are crystalline forms of the element sulphur made of S₈ rings packed differently; the transition temperature is 96 °C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Sulphur(IV) oxide is passed into water and the solution is tested. The solution
questions.A: turns blue litmus red because it contains trioxosulphate(IV) acid
questions.B: turns red litmus blue because it is alkaline
questions.explanation: SO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂SO₃, a weak acid; SO₂ is an acidic oxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The general formula of the alkynes is
questions.explanation: Alkynes contain one triple bond and have four fewer hydrogens than the corresponding alkane: e.g. C₂H₂, C₃H₄.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A compound with the structure CH₃CH₂CH₂CHO gives a silver mirror when warmed with Tollens' reagent. The compound is
questions.explanation: The –CHO group at the end of a four-carbon chain makes it an aldehyde (butanal); aldehydes reduce Tollens' reagent to silver.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A reagent bottle in the laboratory shows the structure CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂OH. The correct IUPAC name to write on its label is
questions.explanation: Number from the end nearer the –OH: the chain is butan-1-ol and the methyl group is on carbon 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: But-1-ene and but-2-ene are examples of
questions.explanation: They have the same carbon skeleton and functional group but differ in the position of the double bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is a functional-group isomer of propanal, CH₃CH₂CHO?
questions.explanation: Propanal and propanone both have the formula C₃H₆O but one is an aldehyde and the other a ketone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ethanoic acid reacts with sodium hydroxide to form
questions.explanation: CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O — a neutralisation, since ethanoic acid is a (weak) acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The reaction between ethanoic acid and ethanol in the presence of concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid produces a compound with a fruity smell. The compound is
questions.explanation: Acid + alcohol → ester + water; ethyl ethanoate, CH₃COOC₂H₅, is the ester.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The alkane that has isomers is
questions.explanation: Butane (C₄H₁₀) exists as n-butane and 2-methylpropane; the three smaller alkanes have only one structure each.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Polythene is formed from ethene by
questions.explanation: Ethene molecules add to one another through their double bonds with no by-product: n CH₂=CH₂ → (–CH₂–CH₂–)ₙ.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements about benzene is correct?
questions.A: it readily decolourises bromine water at room temperature
questions.B: all six C–C bonds are of the same length
questions.D: it contains three isolated double bonds
questions.explanation: The six π electrons are delocalised round the ring, so every bond is intermediate between single and double (0.139 nm).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ethanol for use as a fuel is produced from cassava or sugar cane by
questions.explanation: Yeast enzymes convert glucose to ethanol and carbon(IV) oxide: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The product obtained when 1 mol of ethyne reacts with 2 mol of hydrogen over a nickel catalyst is
questions.explanation: Both π bonds of the triple bond are hydrogenated: C₂H₂ + 2H₂ → C₂H₆.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A kerosene stove with a badly adjusted wick burns with a yellow, smoky flame and blackens the bottom of the pot. The black deposit forms because
questions.A: the kerosene contains a lot of dissolved carbon powder
questions.B: the fuel burns incompletely in a limited supply of air, leaving unburnt carbon
questions.C: the pot reacts with the hot kerosene vapour to form soot
questions.D: the flame is too hot and decomposes the metal of the pot
questions.explanation: With insufficient oxygen a hydrocarbon burns incompletely, forming carbon (soot) and carbon(II) oxide instead of only CO₂ and water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a secondary alcohol?
questions.explanation: In propan-2-ol the carbon carrying the –OH is bonded to two other carbon atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than alkanes of similar molecular mass because
questions.A: carboxylic acid molecules are much heavier
questions.B: carboxylic acid molecules form hydrogen bonds with one another
questions.explanation: Pairs of –COOH groups hydrogen-bond into dimers, so far more energy is needed to separate the molecules than for non-polar alkanes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A gaseous hydrocarbon decolourises bromine water, has the empirical formula CH₂ and a vapour density of 28. The hydrocarbon is (C = 12, H = 1)
questions.explanation: Relative molecular mass = 2 × 28 = 56; (CH₂)ₙ: 14n = 56, so n = 4: C₄H₈, butene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Temporary hardness in water is caused by dissolved
questions.explanation: Ca(HCO₃)₂ decomposes on boiling to insoluble CaCO₃, which is why this hardness can be removed by boiling.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Kettles used to boil hard water develop a white deposit (fur) because
questions.A: the water evaporates and leaves the dissolved sodium chloride behind
questions.B: calcium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV) decomposes to insoluble calcium trioxocarbonate(IV)
questions.C: the metal of the kettle corrodes and forms a white layer of metal oxide
questions.D: the soap dissolved in the water forms a scum that sticks to the element
questions.explanation: Ca(HCO₃)₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ on heating; the insoluble trioxocarbonate(IV) coats the element.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Water is softened by passing it through an ion-exchange resin. The resin removes hardness by
questions.A: filtering out the calcium salts as solid particles
questions.B: replacing calcium and magnesium ions with sodium ions
questions.C: boiling the water inside the column to remove the salts
questions.D: adding chlorine that destroys the calcium and magnesium ions
questions.explanation: Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions are held by the resin and Na⁺ ions are released; sodium salts do not form scum.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Chlorine is added to municipal water supplies in order to
questions.explanation: Chlorine (or oxochlorate(I) ions) disinfects the water; coagulation and filtration handle the suspended solids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The percentage by volume of oxygen in clean dry air is approximately
questions.explanation: Air is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 0.9% argon and 0.04% carbon(IV) oxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A candle burning in a closed jar over water goes out after a while and the water level rises about one-fifth of the way up the jar. This shows that
questions.A: the air is about one-fifth oxygen
questions.B: the candle produces water vapour only
questions.C: carbon(IV) oxide is lighter than air
questions.explanation: The oxygen (about 21% of the air) is used up and the CO₂ formed largely dissolves, so the water rises to replace the oxygen consumed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The main gas responsible for the greenhouse effect and global warming is
questions.explanation: CO₂ (with methane and water vapour) absorbs infrared radiation emitted by the Earth and traps heat in the atmosphere.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The layer of ozone in the upper atmosphere is important because it
questions.A: supplies oxygen for breathing at high altitude
questions.B: absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun
questions.C: reflects radio waves back to the Earth
questions.D: traps heat and keeps the Earth warm
questions.explanation: Ozone (O₃) absorbs most of the Sun's UV-B radiation, which would otherwise cause skin cancer and crop damage.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) released from old refrigerators damage the environment mainly by
questions.explanation: UV light releases chlorine atoms from CFCs, and each chlorine atom catalyses the destruction of thousands of ozone molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Water is described as the universal solvent because
questions.A: it dissolves every known substance completely at room temperature
questions.B: its polar molecules dissolve a wide range of ionic and polar substances
questions.C: it is the most abundant liquid on Earth and is found in every solution
questions.D: it has a neutral pH, so it reacts with neither acids nor bases
questions.explanation: The polar O–H bonds and hydrogen bonding let water surround and separate ions and polar molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following pollutants is produced mainly by the incomplete combustion of petrol in car engines?
questions.explanation: With limited oxygen the carbon in the fuel is oxidised only as far as CO, a colourless, odourless and poisonous gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Fertiliser washed from farms into a lake makes the water green with algae; the fish later die because
questions.A: the fertiliser is directly poisonous to fish
questions.B: decaying algae use up the dissolved oxygen in the water
questions.C: the algae eat the fish eggs
questions.explanation: This is eutrophication: bacteria decomposing the dead algal bloom consume dissolved oxygen, suffocating fish and other aquatic life.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Distilled water does not conduct electricity appreciably because it
questions.C: is a covalent liquid that cannot be electrolysed
questions.explanation: Pure water is only very slightly ionised (about 10⁻⁷ mol/dm³ of H⁺ and OH⁻); tap water conducts because of dissolved salts.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the Contact process the reaction 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ is carried out at about 450 °C and 1–2 atm with a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst. A high pressure is NOT used because
questions.A: high pressure would decompose the vanadium(V) oxide catalyst
questions.B: the yield is already about 98% at low pressure, so the extra cost is not justified
questions.C: high pressure shifts this equilibrium to the left and lowers the yield
questions.D: sulphur(VI) oxide would solidify in the pipes at high pressure
questions.explanation: Although higher pressure would favour SO₃ slightly, the conversion is already almost complete under mild conditions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The products of the Solvay process are sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) and
questions.explanation: Overall: 2NaCl + CaCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + CaCl₂; the ammonia is recycled.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Nitrogen for the Haber process is obtained from
questions.B: the fractional distillation of liquid air
questions.explanation: Air is liquefied and its components separated by their boiling points (N₂ −196 °C, O₂ −183 °C).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the manufacture of trioxonitrate(V) acid by the Ostwald process, ammonia is first
questions.A: dissolved in water to form ammonium hydroxide
questions.B: oxidised over a platinum catalyst to nitrogen(II) oxide
questions.C: reduced to nitrogen gas over an iron catalyst
questions.D: reacted with tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid to form a salt
questions.explanation: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O at about 900 °C over Pt/Rh; the NO is then oxidised to NO₂ and absorbed in water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Soap is made by boiling palm oil with concentrated sodium hydroxide solution. This reaction is called
questions.explanation: The alkali hydrolyses the fat (an ester) into glycerol and the sodium salts of the fatty acids, which are the soap.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Common salt is added to the mixture at the end of soap making in order to
questions.A: give the soap a pleasant smell and taste
questions.B: reduce the solubility of the soap so that it separates out
questions.C: make the soap lather better in hard water
questions.D: neutralise the excess alkali left in the mixture
questions.explanation: Salting out: soap is less soluble in brine, so it rises to the surface and can be skimmed off from the glycerol solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a natural polymer?
questions.explanation: Starch is a polymer of glucose made by plants; the others are synthetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Petrol, kerosene and diesel are obtained from crude oil by
questions.explanation: The fractions are separated in a tall column according to their boiling-point ranges.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A fraction of crude oil that boils at a higher temperature than petrol consists of hydrocarbons that
questions.A: have shorter carbon chains and are more flammable
questions.B: have longer carbon chains and are more viscous
questions.C: contain more hydrogen per carbon atom
questions.explanation: Boiling point rises with chain length as van der Waals forces increase; longer chains also flow less easily and ignite less readily.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The setting of cement after water is added is mainly the result of
questions.A: evaporation of the water from the wet mixture
questions.B: hydration reactions forming interlocking crystals of calcium silicates
questions.C: the cement powder dissolving completely in the water added
questions.D: reaction of the cement with oxygen and carbon(IV) oxide in the air
questions.explanation: Cement hardens chemically, not by drying — it will set even under water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements about soapless detergents is correct?
questions.A: they are made from animal fats by boiling with caustic soda
questions.B: they are usually made from petroleum products and do not form scum in hard water
questions.C: they cannot remove grease from clothes
questions.explanation: The sulphonate salts in soapless detergents have soluble calcium and magnesium salts, so they lather in hard water; some branched-chain types resist bacterial breakdown.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Nitrogenous fertilisers such as urea and ammonium tetraoxosulphate(VI) are applied to crops because nitrogen is needed for
questions.D: raising the pH of the soil
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is a component of amino acids, proteins and chlorophyll; a deficiency gives yellow, stunted plants.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Glucose reduces Fehling's or Benedict's solution because its molecule contains
questions.explanation: The –CHO group of glucose is oxidised to –COOH while Cu²⁺ is reduced to the brick-red Cu₂O precipitate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The bond that links amino acids together in a protein chain is the
questions.explanation: The –COOH group of one amino acid condenses with the –NH₂ group of the next to form a –CO–NH– peptide link, releasing water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Starch and cellulose are both polymers of glucose, yet cotton (cellulose) cannot be digested by humans while starch can. The difference is in
questions.A: the number of glucose units in each polymer chain
questions.B: the way the glucose units are linked (α in starch, β in cellulose)
questions.C: the elements present in each of the two polymers
questions.D: the solubility of the glucose units in water
questions.explanation: Human amylase hydrolyses only the α-1,4 glycosidic links of starch.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A fat that is solid at room temperature differs from an oil that is liquid mainly in that the fat
questions.A: contains more unsaturated fatty acid chains
questions.B: contains more saturated fatty acid chains
questions.explanation: Saturated chains pack closely and have higher melting points; the C=C bonds in unsaturated oils prevent close packing.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The iodine number of an oil is a measure of its
questions.explanation: Iodine adds across C=C double bonds; the more unsaturated the oil, the greater the mass of iodine absorbed per 100 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the monomer of natural rubber?
questions.explanation: Natural rubber latex is poly(isoprene); vulcanising with sulphur cross-links the chains and makes it harder.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Maltose is hydrolysed by dilute acid to give
questions.explanation: Maltose is a disaccharide made of two glucose units; sucrose gives glucose + fructose and lactose gives glucose + galactose.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the Millon's test a protein sample gives
questions.explanation: Millon's reagent reacts with the tyrosine in proteins to give a red coloration; blue-black is the starch–iodine test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Enzymes are described as biological catalysts because they
questions.A: are used up as the reaction proceeds
questions.B: speed up reactions in living cells and remain unchanged at the end
questions.C: provide the energy for the reactions of the cell
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins that lower the activation energy of specific reactions and are regenerated after each turnover.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Vegetable oil is hardened into margarine by hydrogenation. The catalyst used is
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is bubbled through the hot oil over nickel at about 180 °C, saturating some of the C=C bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements about amino acids is correct?
questions.A: they contain only carbon and hydrogen
questions.B: each contains both an amino group and a carboxyl group
questions.C: they are all obtained from carbohydrates
questions.explanation: The –NH₂ and –COOH groups on the same molecule make amino acids amphoteric and let them link into proteins.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar, but after boiling with dilute acid the solution reduces Benedict's solution. The acid has
questions.A: oxidised the sucrose to an acid
questions.B: hydrolysed the sucrose to glucose and fructose
questions.explanation: Inversion: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ + H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ (glucose) + C₆H₁₂O₆ (fructose), both of which are reducing sugars.
